title: 1989 AHSME Problem 9
statement: Mr. and Mrs. Zeta want to name their baby Zeta so that its monogram (first, middle, and last initials) will be in alphabetical order with no letters repeated. How many such monograms are possible?

solutions.text:
The first two initials must be two distinct letters chosen from \(A\) through \(Y.\) Once chosen, their order is forced. Therefore the number of monograms is \[ \binom{25}{2}=300. \]

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: The last initial is already fixed as \(Z\)
Choosing the other two distinct letters determines their alphabetical order
